title: The Iron Harbor
premise: In 1917, at the besieged port of Vela Cruz, battlefield nurse Rafael Oyelaran secretly records in his ledger the names of soldiers the military bureaucracy erases—deserters executed, civilians 'requisitioned,' a massacre at the fish market. When a dying officer presses a sealed letter into his hands, Rafael discovers his own family is implicated in the plot it documents, and that the ledger itself is evidence worth killing for. Over six desperate days he must move the letter and ledger past three checkpoints with the help of a conflicted garrison officer, Captain Ilsa Brandt, who must choose between her oath and the truth. In the end Rafael smuggles the evidence onto a neutral ship, but only by surrendering his own name to the authorities—surviving, yet erased, until the ledger's copies surface years later and his family's honor is posthumously restored.
about_author: Petra Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing military correspondence from coastal garrisons, where she first encountered ledgers kept by unofficial record-keepers. She writes historical fiction from a restored harbor house, drawn to stories of people history tried to leave out.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings In
chapters.summary: Rafael tends the wounded at the harbor infirmary while recording omitted names in his hidden ledger, establishing his quiet system of remembrance. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: weary tenderness masking a simmering anger at institutional erasure.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Blank Line
chapters.summary: A requisition order empties the fish-market quarter; Rafael treats the displaced and logs a massacre the official report calls 'collateral clearing.' POV: Rafael, with a brief interlude from his sister Amara's letters. Emotional beat: grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Captain Brandt's Signature
chapters.summary: Rafael meets Captain Ilsa Brandt when she countersigns death lists; she notices his careful corrections and says nothing—yet. POV: Ilsa, revealing her duty-bound interior and her own doubts. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two careful people.

chapters.title: A Letter, Sealed in Blood
chapters.summary: A dying officer, Lieutenant Corso, presses a sealed letter into Rafael's hands with the words 'the family knows.' Rafael hides it inside his ledger. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: fear arriving like cold water—the letter names the Oyelaran family.

chapters.title: Names My Mother Chose
chapters.summary: Rafael deciphers enough of the letter to learn his family is implicated in the fish-market plot as scapegoats for a commander's theft. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the personal detonating inside the political; invisibility is over.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One Harbor
chapters.summary: Rafael maps his route: the garrison gate, the customs house, the quay. Each checkpoint demands papers he cannot forge alone. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: cold planning as a form of hope.

chapters.title: The Forger of Rope Street
chapters.summary: Rafael seeks out Tomás, a disgraced clerk who forges passes, paying with the last of his savings and a dangerous favor owed. POV: Tomás, a new voice—cowardly, funny, terrified. Emotional beat: unlikely alliance born of mutual leverage.

chapters.title: What Duty Weighs
chapters.summary: Ilsa is ordered to find Corso's missing letter before it reaches 'foreign hands'; she realizes the search will destroy innocents. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the first crack in her oath.

chapters.title: Amara's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Rafael visits his family under watch; soldiers have already searched the house. His mother burns letters, not knowing which ones mattered. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: love as a liability he can no longer set down.

chapters.title: The Ledger Speaks
chapters.summary: Rafael shows Tomás the ledger to prove the stakes; Tomás recognizes a name—his brother, listed among the executed deserters. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: the forger's cynicism shattering; he commits fully.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Garrison Gate
chapters.summary: Rafael makes his first run with forged papers; a sergeant who once owed Corso waves him through—but Ilsa watches from a window and recognizes his gait. POV: Rafael, ending on Ilsa's suspicion. Emotional beat: triumph laced with dread.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Ilsa summons Rafael for questioning; he lies skillfully, and she lets him go—deliberately, she later admits to herself. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: love against duty, choosing the man over the order without yet admitting why.

chapters.title: The Neutral Ship
chapters.summary: Rafael negotiates with Marta, a smuggler captain, to carry the evidence out on the Dutch freighter Vrijheid, sailing in four days. POV: Marta, pragmatic and unsentimental. Emotional beat: hope with a price tag and a deadline.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Infirmary
chapters.summary: A fellow nurse, pressured by the commander's agents, reports Rafael's midnight copying of documents; Tomás is arrested instead. POV: Rafael, helpless. Emotional beat: guilt and the cost of trusting anyone.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Rafael must reach Tomás's hidden duplicate passes before the customs inspection; he trades his mother's ring to a bribable inspector. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: survival measured in what can be carried—and what must be left.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Choice
chapters.summary: Ilsa finds the ledger's existence confirmed and the commander's theft documented; she confronts him privately and is threatened with her own court-martial. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: duty inverted—the loyal act is now the treasonous one.

chapters.title: The Cell Below
chapters.summary: Rafael visits Tomás in the stockade under pretense of medical duty; Tomás gives him the last pass and tells him to run without him. POV: Tomás. Emotional beat: sacrifice freely given; grief refused the time to be felt.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Quay
chapters.summary: Dawn, fog, and the final barrier. Ilsa appears at the quay—not to arrest Rafael but to countersign his papers with her own name, sealing her fate. POV: alternating Rafael and Ilsa. Emotional beat: love declared in the language of risk.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: Soldiers close in as the Vrijheid loads; Rafael realizes he cannot board with the letter without dooming the ship to search. He gives the ledger's copies to Marta and stays behind as decoy. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—his freedom for the truth's escape.

chapters.title: The Name He Surrenders
chapters.summary: Rafael is arrested; under interrogation he claims sole authorship of the ledger, shielding Ilsa and his family. The commander needs a scapegoat more than a trial. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: erasure chosen willingly—the inverse of his life's work.

chapters.title: The Ship That Carried the Names
chapters.summary: The Vrijheid clears the harbor; months later the ledger reaches a foreign newspaper, forcing an inquiry. Ilsa, reassigned in disgrace, sends Rafael one line: 'They are reading them aloud.' POV: Ilsa and Marta. Emotional beat: vindication arriving too slowly to feel like victory, but arriving.

chapters.title: Ledger, Open
chapters.summary: Years later, a pardoned Rafael walks the rebuilt fish-market quarter as names from his ledger are carved into a memorial wall; Amara reads their mother's name aloud. He and Ilsa meet again at the harbor's edge. POV: Rafael. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace—identity restored not by the state, but by the names themselves.
